import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1138

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1138](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1138)
- [Va99] Vardi, I., Prime census. (1999).
- [Kum26] Kumrawat, S., [Disproof of Erdős Problem 1138](https://sourish-kumrawat.github.io/papers/Erdos_1138.pdf).

Note that the conjecture has a claimed disproof found at:
https://sourish-kumrawat.github.io/papers/Erdos_1138.pdf,
see the discussion section on the Erdos problems website for more information.
-/

open Nat Filter Asymptotics Real Set

namespace Erdos1138

/--
The maximal prime gap below $x$, i.e. $d(x) = \max_{p_n < x}(p_{n+1} - p_n)$, where $p_n$
denotes the $n$-th prime.
-/
noncomputable def sup_primeGap (x : ℝ) : ℕ := (Finset.range (primeCounting' ⌈x⌉₊)).sup primeGap

/--
The filter on $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}$ corresponding to sending $x \to \infty$ subject to $x/2 < y < x$
-/
abbrev snd_gt_half_fst : Filter (ℝ × ℝ) := atTop.comap Prod.fst ⊓ 𝓟 {p | p.2 ∈ Ioo (p.1 / 2) p.1}

/-- Given a pair $(x,y)$, this is the amount of primes in the interval above $y$, of length
equalling the largest prime gap before $x$, scaled by a constant $C$.
-/
noncomputable def primeCount_Ioc_mul_const (C : ℝ) : (ℝ × ℝ) → ℝ :=
  fun (x, y) ↦ (primeCounting ⌊y + C * sup_primeGap x⌋₊ - primeCounting ⌊y⌋₊)

/--
**Erdős Problem 1138.**
Let $x/2 < y < x$ and $C > 1$. If $d = \max_{p_n < x}(p_{n+1} - p_n)$,
where $p_n$ denotes the $n$-th prime, then is it true that
$$\pi(y + Cd) - \pi(y) \sim \frac{Cd}{\log y}$$?
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/YanYablonovskiy/formal-conjectures/blob/7c134317104d3b98ecc751afbb79ec0adddf8e7c/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/1138a.lean#L496"]
theorem erdos_1138 : answer(False) ↔ ∀C > 1,
    primeCount_Ioc_mul_const C ~[snd_gt_half_fst] fun (x, y) ↦
      C * (sup_primeGap x) / Real.log y := by
  sorry

end Erdos1138

findings.description: The module bibliography identifies [Va99] as “Vardi, I., Prime census. (1999).” This does not match the reference [Va99,1.3] used by the cited Erdős problem page: that reference denotes a conference problem booklet by Various, not the stated Vardi work. The mathematical declarations themselves are unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/1138 cites [Va99,1.3]. Its bibliography entry at https://www.erdosproblems.com/bibs/Va99 reads: “Various, Some of Paul's favorite problems. Booklet produced for the conference ‘Paul Erdős and his mathematics’, Budapest, July 1999 (1999).”
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the [Va99] entry with: “Various, Some of Paul's favorite problems. Booklet produced for the conference ‘Paul Erdős and his mathematics’, Budapest, July 1999 (1999), §1.3.”

reformulations.difference: The indexed maximum over primes below a real number is implemented as a finite supremum over zero-based indices below primeCounting' ⌈x⌉₊.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved in Lean that n ∈ Finset.range (primeCounting' ⌈x⌉₊) iff (Nat.nth Nat.Prime n : ℝ) < x, and proved the corresponding maximum upper-bound characterization. Consecutive primes are strictly increasing, so natural subtraction gives their ordinary gap. This includes gaps whose right endpoint exceeds x, exactly as the source requires. The value 0 for x ≤ 2 is an irrelevant totalization outside the asymptotic tail.

reformulations.difference: The source's real-argument prime-counting difference is implemented using natural floors and real casts of natural prime counts.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For C ≥ 0, proved that the definition equals the real-valued cardinality of primesLE ⌊y + C*d(x)⌋₊ \ primesLE ⌊y⌋₊. Separately proved that membership in this difference is equivalent to primality together with y < p ≤ y + C*d(x). Thus the lower endpoint is excluded and the upper endpoint included, as in π(y+Cd)−π(y). Natural-floor behavior at negative arguments introduces no primes and causes no discrepancy.

reformulations.difference: The uniform asymptotic for each fixed C is expressed through IsEquivalent along the two-variable filter snd_gt_half_fst, and the negative answer is encoded as False ↔ ∀ C > 1, ….
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved that eventual P along snd_gt_half_fst means exactly ∃ X, ∀ x ≥ X, ∀ y, x/2 < y → y < x → P(x,y). The filter is nontrivial, y tends to infinity, and C*d(x)/log y is eventually positive for C > 1; therefore IsEquivalent is equivalent to the quotient tending to 1. Also proved the full statement equivalent to the negation of the explicit uniform epsilon–threshold assertion. The negation is of validity for every fixed C > 1, not failure for every individual C, matching Corollary 1 of the disproof and the source discussion.
